data.title: WiseTech Global Oct. CargoWise Revenue Rises, Says Confident To Meet FY27 Targets; Shares Climb
data.description:
CANBERA (dpa-AFX) - WiseTech Global Limited (WTC.AX), a provider of software solutions and logistics executions, Friday announced that it is confident to achieve fiscal 2027 targets based on performance to the end of October, and subject to the momentum and continuing favorable market conditions.

In its trading update, the company said year-to-date October CargoWise revenue grew 11%, driven by higher transaction volumes, growth from LGFF and STL price increases. Costs are tracking in line with expectations.

Following the news, the shares gained around 15% in Australian trading on Friday, closing at A$53.87.

For the full year, the company continues to expect underlying EBITDA range of $725 million to $780 million and revenue of $1.48 billion to $1.5 billion. Underlying EBITDA margin would be 49% to 51%, a growth of 3 to 5 percentage points year-over-year.

The annual outlook reflects underlying EBITDA growth ranging from 12 percent to 21 percent over a year ago, and revenue growth of 6 percent to 10 percent over prior year.

WiseTech noted that in August, its revenue guidance was predicated on modest adoption of key initiatives to achieve the bottom of guidance range, with those key initiatives second half weighted.

The company said the outlook confirmation is even before the adoption of the growth initiatives announced earlier.

WiseTech said it enter fiscal 2027 with a number of important goals that are tied to long-term strategy and vision, and that respond to the opportunities in the disruption currently seeing in the software sector generally from advancements in AI.

The company also said that it entered the new year with more growth opportunities across the business than ever before, a lower cost base, stronger margins, strong cash flow and a deleveraging plan that is ahead of schedule.

Further, AI Transformation delivered about $51 million of annualized EBITDA run-rate savings in fiscal 2026, and the firm expects a further $40 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of fiscal 2027, with net savings of $10 million in the year.

Regarding the adoption of AI, the company said more than 90% of its code is now written or assisted by AI. Engineering productivity is up 57%, compared with 45% at the end of fiscal 2026.

AI, and its impact on the operating models of WiseTech and customers, has been an important part of the Company's strategy since 2022, the firm said.

data.title: Asian stocks jump on U.S. futures rally, China profit beats, shrugging off tariff risks
data.description:
Asian equity markets traded higher on Friday, buoyed by a strong rally in U.S. stock futures ahead of Wall Street’s shortened post-Thanksgiving session. Renewed momentum in the artificial intelligence trade, sparked by late-Wednesday dip-buying, helped lift sentiment across the region.

Japan’s Nikkei 225 climbed 2.12% to above 58,700.00, with the Japanese yen . South Korea’s benchmark KOSPI jumped 4.23% to 4,910.47. Meanwhile, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index () up 2.05% to 22,685.50, and mainland China’s Shanghai Composite () rose 2.95% to 3,576.45, while the Shenzhen Component rose 4.86% to 10,573.03. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 () rose 0.80% to 8,833.60. The Australian dollar rose toward $0.67, climbing off a one-year low.

On the macroeconomic front, Beijing rejected U.S. allegations of industrial "overcapacity" as a "false premise" and vowed to defend its interests, as it faces a 20% U.S. tariff that could rise to 40% if Washington deems trade efforts insufficient. Supporting domestic sentiment, however, data showed Chinese industrial profits rose 16.0% Y/Y to CNY 6.74T in the first ten months of 2026, accelerating from 15.5% growth in the January–September period.

Core consumer prices in Tokyo’s central wards increased 2.9% Y/Y in November 2026, up from 2.6% in October, though slightly below the 3.0% consensus forecast.

Australia’s Canberra’s new Domestic Gas Reservation Scheme, requiring LNG exporters to reserve up to 20% of exports for domestic supply starting January 2028, bolstered expectations for lower energy costs.

In commodities, gold prices climbed above $3,600 an ounce, while crude oil climbed above $85 per barrel.

U.S. stock futures jumped on Friday as markets reopened following the Thanksgiving holiday, with markets looking to build on the pre-holiday dip-buying that emerged late Wednesday amid renewed strength in the artificial intelligence trade.

data.title: Coforge shares rebound 3.5% after Advent International dismisses speculation over imminent stake sale
data.description:
Shares of Coforge Ltd rose 3.5 percent to Rs 2,070 in morning trade on Friday, November 27, recovering their previous session's losses after private equity firm Advent International dismissed speculation over an imminent stake sale in the IT services company.

Coforge shares had plunged around 6 percent in intraday trade on Thursday to hit a nearly one-month low of Rs 1,945.6 after a media report said entities owned by Advent International were looking to offload around 10 percent stake in the company through block deals. The stock subsequently recovered some of its losses to settle 2.91 percent lower at Rs 2,000 on Thursday.

No block deal in Coforge shares had been reported as of Friday morning.

Advent International dismisses stake sale speculation

CNBC-TV18 reported on Thursday, citing unidentified sources, that entities owned by Advent International were likely to sell around 10 percent stake in Coforge through block deals to institutional investors. Two investment banks had reportedly been appointed to manage the proposed transaction, which was expected to take place soon.

  • Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today

However, Advent International later clarified that it remained a committed and active shareholder in Coforge. The US-based private equity firm also termed the speculation regarding imminent block trade transactions in the IT services company as unfounded.

Entities owned by Advent International currently hold around 20 percent stake in Coforge. At the company's current market capitalisation of around Rs 91,700 crore, a 10 percent stake would be valued at approximately Rs 9,170 crore.

Advent's share lock-in period to expire on November 30

The speculation over a potential stake sale comes ahead of the expiry of the mandatory six-month lock-in period on Advent International's shares in Coforge on November 30. Coforge had allotted the shares to Advent International on a preferential basis at Rs 1,815.91 apiece in April. The allotment followed the IT services company's announcement in December 2025 that it would acquire Encora at an enterprise value of $2.35 billion.

At Friday's prevailing market price, Coforge shares were trading around 14 percent above the preferential allotment price.

While the expiry of the lock-in period would enable Advent International to sell its shares, it does not necessarily imply an immediate stake dilution.

Coforge share price performance

Coforge shares have gained around 25 percent so far in 2026, significantly outperforming the benchmark Nifty 50, which has declined around 1.1 percent during the same period. Friday's rebound has also taken the stock marginally above Wednesday's closing price of Rs 2,060, erasing the losses triggered by the stake sale report.

data.title: Shares bounce after bruising month, dollar on course for third monthly gain
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nikkei up 2.1%, Nasdaq futures climb 2.4%
  • Chinese stocks jump almost 4% on new support measures
  • Dollar set for 1.7% monthly gain against major peers

By Stella Qiu

Asian shares steadied on Friday as they neared the end of a bruising month with a holiday lull giving some respite from AI jitters, while the dollar rode a wave of safe-haven demand and rate hike bets towards a third month of gains.

Wall Street shut on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday, but Nasdaq futures rallied 2.4% and S&P 500 futures were 1.7% higher. European bourses are set to extend the rally, with benchmark stock futures up 0.7%.

Japan's Nikkei jumped 2.1%, bringing to 4% its gains for the week, as it clawed back some of its 7.2% loss over the month.

Friday data showed core inflation in Tokyo hit a 16-month high in November, bolstering the case for an interest rate hike from the Bank of Japan as soon as next month.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MIAPJ0000PUS) jumped 1.7% to end the week 1.6% higher, but was still down 7.2% for the month.

Shares in South Korea surged 4% and China's blue chips gained 3.8% a day after hitting their lowest since June 2025, as the cabinet rolled out more support for capital markets.

"It is quite possible that the rebound could go further," said Shane Oliver, chief economist at AMP.

He cited factors such as the return of Jensen Huang to chipmaker Nvidia, the resilient US economy, strong corporate profit growth and December being a seasonally stronger period for shares.

"However, the risk of a deeper correction at some point in the next six months remains high."

However, Nvidia stayed a source of unease after S&P put its credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade.

The company told manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers containing its chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, the Financial Times said.

Elsewhere in tech, Elon Musk promised every US child two shares in his space and AI company SpaceX , for a total gift worth about $18 billion.

Oil prices were headed for the first weekly rise in four on renewed concerns about supply disruptions. Brent crude futures rose 0.3% on Friday to $96.85 a barrel, and were up 4.6% for the week. For the month, they were down nearly 18%.

DOLLAR REIGNS

The US dollar was headed for its third monthly gain on Friday, up 1.7% against major peers at 103.8, supported by expectations that the Federal Reserve is almost certain to lift interest rates in December, as well as safe-haven flows from an equities selloff.

Futures imply a 99% chance the Fed will raise rates by 25 basis points in December, but speculation of a half-point increase has faded. (0#USDIRPR)

The euro was up 0.1% at $1.0980 after news that Spanish central banking veteran Pablo Hernández de Cos would become the next president of the European Central Bank, a well-telegraphed move that suggested policy continuity.

The kiwi edged up 0.4% to $0.5482 after New Zealand's ruling centre-right coalition fell short of a parliamentary majority, som that it will have to resort to talks with the centrist Opportunity Party to retain power.

Bond investors are wondering if this month's broad losses in global stocks, coupled with doubts about the durability of AI-driven business investment, might make central banks less hawkish.

"The Fed could, of course, still blink," said David Rees, chief economist at Schroders. "But a Fed put would not necessarily be unambiguously positive for markets."

"If growth and inflation data remain firm, in a game of cat and mouse markets could soon begin pricing a more hawkish Fed back in, potentially setting off the same chain of events all over again."

The stocks rally drove down Treasuries, with two-year yields (US2YT=RR) rising 5 basis points to 4.6891% as the cash market reopened after the US holiday. They were up 8 bps this week.

Benchmark 10-year Treasury yields rose 7 bps to 4.9156%, but were flat at 2 bps for the week.

data.title: Asian Markets Rise as AI Sentiment Stabilizes — Update
data.description:
By Sherry Qin and Kimberley Kao

Asian markets rose on Friday, tracking gains in U.S. stock futures as sentiment around the artificial intelligence trade stabilized.

"With U.S. bourses shut for Thanksgiving, global stocks mostly rose in the absence of cues," Maybank analysts said in a note.

That has left "markets to trade largely off the late recovery on Wall Street in Wednesday's session," said Westpac's Neha Sharma in an email.

Regional investors took cues from stronger U.S. futures. E-mini Nasdaq futures were up 2.6%, while contracts tied to the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 1.7% and 1.1%, respectively.

South Korea's Kospi rose 4.2%, with chip heavyweights SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics jumping 6.3% and 4.2%, respectively.

Japan's Nikkei Stock Average advanced 2.0%. SoftBank Group was last 3.7% higher, while chip players Resonac Holdings and Advantest surged 9.7% and 6.0% respectively.

The gains came even as Nvidia ordered its manufacturing partners to pause shipments to four Southeast Asian countries, after the U.S. escalated its push to keep the company's AI chips out of China's hands, The Wall Street Journal reported.

Meanwhile, China's State Council on Friday reinforced its support for the capital market and stressed the need to improve market-stabilizing mechanisms. It also said that listed companies should be encouraged to pay more dividends and step up share repurchases.

China's Shanghai Composite Index rose 3.2%, while tech-heavy ChiNext Price Index jumped 10%, keeping it on track for its biggest one-day gain in over two years.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was 2.3% higher, while the Hang Seng Tech Index rose 6.3% and Taiwan's Taiex was up by 0.4%.

The three-month LME copper contract jumped 4.6% to $12,423.00 a ton. Copper prices are supported by strong near-term AI spending expectations, according to ANZ research analysts in a commentary. Copper is a key metal for data center development.

Spot gold rose 2.0% to $3,638.54 a troy ounce while spot silver rose 5.0% to $43.60 a troy ounce. Bitcoin rose 1.6%.

Oil prices jumped on fresh concerns of a re-escalation of tensions in the Middle East. Iran has stepped up its strikes, targeting some of its Gulf neighbors and ships trying to get oil and natural gas through the Strait of Hormuz. Most recently, an Iranian drone attack on Kuwait killed two Italians performing maintenance on antidrone equipment, authorities said.

Meanwhile, Yemen's Houthi militant group attacked Saudi Arabia's Jazan oil refinery on Thursday and killed one worker, the kingdom's Ministry of Energy said in a statement.

The attacks offset hopes of a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, ANZ Research analysts said in a note.

However, U.S. commercial crude oil inventories rose for a third consecutive week in the seven days through Nov. 20, while gasoline and distillate stockpiles also increased, according to the latest data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

Front-month West Texas Intermediate crude-oil futures rose 3.3% to $86.43 a barrel, while front-month Brent was up 0.9% at $97.41 a barrel, according to ICE data.

Write to Sherry Qin at sherry.qin@wsj.com

data.title: Coal India arm Mahanadi Coalfields makes muted market debut; shares fall 2%
data.description:
Shares of Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd, a subsidiary of state-owned Coal India, on Friday made a muted market debut, listing with a discount of 2 per cent against the issue price of ₹136.

The stock started trading at ₹133.15, down 2 per cent from the issue price on the BSE.

At the NSE, the stock made its market debut at ₹134, registering a discount of 1.47 per cent.

The company's market valuation stood at ₹90,340.65 crore.

The initial public offering of Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd was fully subscribed on the final day of bidding on Monday.

The ₹8,981-crore IPO was subscribed 1.52 times.

The IPO price band was at ₹129-136 per share.

The Initial Public Offering (IPO) was entirely an offer-for-sale (OFS).

MCL is the third Coal India subsidiary to tap the public markets this year. Coal India has already listed Bharat Coking Coal Ltd in January, while the IPO of Central Mine Planning & Design Institute Ltd concluded in March.

Incorporated in 1992, MCL produced 218.31 million tonnes of coal in FY26, accounting for around 22.4 per cent of India's total non-coking coal production, according to the Crisil report cited in the offer documents.

It is also the largest coal-producing subsidiary of Coal India, contributing over 28 per cent to the state-owned company's total coal production in FY26.

Coal India accounts for more than 80 per cent of the country's domestic coal output.

data.title: Binance Announces Dividends for Nvidia and Other Stocks
data.description:
Binance will pay dividends to holders of stock tokens representing five companies: Nvidia, PayPal, Qualcomm, Western Digital, and Wendy’s.

The exchange will use the dividends paid by these companies to buy more stock tokens, allowing users to increase their holdings of the same stocks through the bStocks program.

The most important date for Nvidia token holders is Dec. 2. That's when Binance will take a snapshot of NVDAB balances at 01:00 UTC.

The snapshot for Wendy’s is scheduled for Dec. 1, followed by Nvidia on Dec. 2 and Qualcomm on Dec. 3.

Snapshots for PayPal and Western Digital are both scheduled for Dec. 4.

All snapshots will take place at 01:00 UTC.

In its Nov. 27 announcement, Binance provided the dates that will determine eligibility for dividends.

How Binance will pay dividends to Nvidia holders

Binance plans to use Nvidia's cash dividends to purchase additional Nvidia shares, including fractional shares, after deducting applicable withholding taxes, fees, and other charges.

The proceeds will then be distributed among users who hold NVDAB on Binance and qualify for the dividend payment.

The same process will apply to the other four stocks.

If you hold eligible tokens in other products on the platform, such as savings or margin accounts, Binance will still credit the dividends to your spot account.

If you hold bStocks on-chain, the dividend payments will be made by adjusting the token's multiplier.

The tokens themselves are issued by Binance affiliate BTECH Holdings Limited, which owns the underlying securities.

So if you hold NVDAB, you have an interest in the Nvidia shares held by BTECH.

If you need to transfer tokens to Binance before the snapshot, you must do so at least two hours in advance.

Deposits and withdrawals of Nvidia tokens will be suspended at 23:00 UTC on Dec. 1.

The balance snapshot will take place at 01:00 UTC on Dec. 2.

Binance will also suspend one-to-one conversions between Nvidia shares and NVDAB tokens during this period.

The same two-hour suspension rule will apply to the other four stock tokens.

However, spot trading against USDT will continue, including trading in the pair.

Binance said it would resume deposits, withdrawals and stock-to-token conversions after the dividend allocations are completed.

The exchange will not issue a separate announcement when these services resume.

data.title: Indonesia considers subsidised fuel price hike as fiscal pressure mounts, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • No final decision taken on whether to hike, nor by how much, sources say
  • Political impact is being considered, one of the sources says
  • Subsidised gasoline, diesel sell far below estimated market prices
  • Last subsidised fuel price hike came in 2022 amid mounting subsidy costs

By Gayatri Suroyo and Stefanno Sulaiman

Indonesia's government is considering raising subsidised fuel prices in early 2027 for the first time in five years, four people familiar with the matter told Reuters, as high global oil prices and a weak rupiah increase pressure on the G20 economy's finances.

Stable fuel prices have played a major part in anchoring inflation at benign levels in Southeast Asia's largest economy, although a string of economic setbacks has driven the rupiah to multiple record lows this year, made Indonesia's stock market the world's worst-performing market, and caused investor confidence to fall fast.

Fuel prices are a particularly sensitive political matter in the world's fourth-most populous country, and hikes have historically been followed by protests. On the political front, polls show President Prabowo Subianto's approval ratings have fallen fast this year, mostly over his handling of the economy.

The price hike proposal was discussed at a meeting last week, attended by officials from Bank Indonesia, state energy company Pertamina, sovereign wealth fund Danantara and the Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs, one source, a state official with direct knowledge of the discussion, told Reuters.

All four sources, two of whom are officials from state-linked institutions involved in the meeting, told Reuters no decision had been reached, and the size of the proposed price hike had not been determined.

The first source said the proposal had come from the state energy company over worries about its financial situation, and factors being weighed included the impacts on Prabowo's popularity and Pertamina's finances.

Indonesia's Government Communication Agency, in response to Reuters queries, said that the government had promised not to raise subsidised fuel prices this year, but, for next year, the president had not given a directive.

The Finance Ministry said through a spokesperson it had no knowledge of any discussion about the future of fuel subsidies. The economic ministry, Bank Indonesia, Danantara, Pertamina and the president's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

FISCAL PRESSURES

Indonesia has kept subsidised fuel prices unchanged despite global oil prices being elevated since conflict in the Middle East disrupted international energy markets. The country's energy subsidy budget is expected to balloon to 500 trillion rupiah ($27.2 billion) this year, 30% higher than originally earmarked.

The finance ministry has already said it could increase the allocation further.

The second source said Pertamina had not received full reimbursements for distributing subsidised fuel, as the government tried to keep its fiscal balance in check.

By law, the government's annual budget deficit is capped at 3% of GDP — a limit that is already being tested by Prabowo's costly flagship programmes, such as distributing free meals to millions of students and pregnant women.

This year's official deficit estimate is 2.85% of GDP.

POLITICAL IMPACT

Fuel price hikes in 1998 contributed to violent demonstrations against then-President Suharto, which ultimately led to his ouster. In 2015, a fuel price hike caused Prabowo's predecessor's approval rating to plummet.

Raising subsidised fuel prices could hurt Prabowo's approval rating as well, said Djayadi Hanan, executive director of pollster Lembaga Survei Indonesia.

"If the public feels economically strained, their assessment of the economic situation will be negative," he said. "When it is negative, it politically leads to public dissatisfaction with the government's performance, especially the president."

With subsidies, 90-octane gasoline is sold at 10,000 rupiah per litre — about $2.1 per gallon - about half its estimated economic price, while diesel is sold at 6,800 rupiah per litre — about $1.4 per gallon — less than a third of its economic price, according to the finance ministry's estimate using October prices.

The subsidy bill has also increased because many buyers who usually consume higher-quality fuel — the price of which has risen periodically — have shifted to subsidised fuel because of the increasing price difference. The energy ministry was considering an increase in the subsidised fuel volume quota, after reports of queues stretching outside fuel stations in several cities.

Indonesia is a net oil importer. The rupiah has fallen to new depths this year and sank to another record low on Thursday of 18,395 to the dollar.

($1 = 18,390.0000 rupiah)

data.title: Hetero close to securing Indian approval for generic Gilead HIV-prevention drug, sources say
data.description:
By Rishika Sadam

Indian drugmaker Hetero is close to securing regulatory approval for a generic version of Gilead Sciences' HIV-prevention drug lenacapavir, two people familiar with the matter told Reuters.

The drug is expected to be launched in India in February, one of the sources said.

India had an estimated 2.56 million people living with HIV in 2024, accounting for about 6.3% of cases worldwide, according to the government’s National AIDS Control Organisation.

Lenacapavir, marketed by Gilead as Yeztugo for HIV prevention, is a long-acting drug administered through twice-yearly injections, offering an alternative to daily oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) pills, although the regimen also includes oral tablets during initiation.

The World Health Organization has recommended lenacapavir as an additional HIV-prevention option after clinical trials showed it was highly effective at preventing infection.

Gilead also markets lenacapavir under a different brand name for treating heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug-resistant HIV.

It was not immediately clear whether Hetero's generic version would also be approved for that use in India.

Hetero had sought approval for both oral and injectable forms of lenacapavir for HIV prevention, the sources said.

Hetero and the Drugs Controller General of India did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

The company said separately on Thursday it had started shipping generic versions of lenacapavir injectable to Africa, with plans to supply 300,000 vials to Zambia, Uganda and Zimbabwe.

Gilead has licensed six generic drugmakers, including Hetero and Dr. Reddy's Laboratories , to manufacture and supply generic lenacapavir in 120 low- and middle-income countries as part of efforts to expand access in regions with high HIV burdens.

data.title: Rupee rally stumbles alongside equities on tentative AI trade comeback
data.description:
By Nimesh Vora

The rupee's rally lost momentum alongside Indian equities on Friday, as a tentative revival in the AI trade threatened to slow the foreign inflows that have supported the currency.

The rupee depreciated to 92.7250 per US dollar by 11:15 a.m. IST after opening slightly weaker near 92.50.

South Korea's AI-heavy market led Asian shares higher, while futures on the Nasdaq index <.NDX> rallied.

A return of appetite for AI-linked shares threatens to slow the flow of foreign money into Indian assets, which has helped fuel the rupee's recovery in recent weeks. India's benchmark Nifty 50 dropped 0.5%.

Foreign investors have net bought around $16 billion worth of Indian stocks in November, reversing a significant portion of the outflows recorded in the first 10 months of the year.

The shift has helped the rupee outperform most of its Asian peers, even as the dollar index hovered near a two-year high. However, a revival in demand for AI-heavy markets could challenge the flow dynamics that have worked in India's favour.

A rise in oil prices acted as another headwind for the rupee on Friday. Brent crude marched towards $96.50 a barrel, reviving concerns over India's import bill.

"Today, you can point to a host of factors to justify the weakness in the rupee, including higher crude prices and the pullback in equities," a currency trader at a bank said.

"However, I think it is the extra bullishness (on the rupee) that is being whittled down, which is leading to the pressure," he added.

Attention will now turn to the Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy decision on December 4. The central bank is widely expected to raise its benchmark rate by 25 basis points, though some economists see some scope for a larger increase, which could support the rupee.

data.title: XPENG-W: Overseas Sales Estimated to Surpass 100,000 Units for First Time This Yr; 5 Models to Launch Overseas Next Yr
data.description:
XPENG-W Vice President Alex revealed at the Auto Guangzhou 2026 that the company's overseas sales were projected to cross 100,000 units for the first time this year. Overseas deliveries in October alone numbered 13,326 units, up 166% YoY. Its global sales and after-sales network now covers 83 countries and regions, with more than 1,300 outlets.

In terms of model performance, the BEV MPV XPENG X9 became the sales champion in Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, New Zealand and Australia. The new technology flagship XPENG GX received more than 5,000 orders within one month of launch in the Middle East and Africa region. Less than two months after its domestic launch, XPENG G9L has already started pre-sales or launched in 25 countries and regions globally.

Since its global launch, overseas orders for the MONA L03 have topped 34,000 units, with deliveries underway simultaneously in Europe, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Latin America. The MONA L05 is set to begin overseas launches, with an expected debut in Thailand in December this year, followed by a Europe-wide launch at the Brussels Motor Show in Europe in Jan next year. Currently, cumulative global deliveries of the MONA series have surpassed 400,000 units, with average monthly deliveries approaching 15,000 units.

In intelligent assisted driving, XPENG's NGP is scheduled for global delivery in 1H27. In terms of charging infrastructure, XPENG's X-Energy megawatt flash charging project will begin deployment in Germany and Australia within three months, establishing the first megawatt flash charging stations in Europe and Australia, further expanding its charging network presence in Europe and the Asia-Pacific market.

data.title: UBS Notes Investor Focus on Div. Hike Potential at CTF SERVICES, Maintains Buy Rating
data.description:
Investors are primarily focused on the potential room for dividend hikes and corporate actions at CTF SERVICES , especially after parent company CTFE committed to underwriting up to 75% of the funding requirement for the rights issue of NEW WORLD DEV , UBS said in a research report.

Some investors were also concerned about the growth outlook for CTF Life, while market feedback on the valuation multiples of recent road asset monetization transactions has generally been positive. Despite the attractive dividend yield, some investors believed relatively low trading liquidity remains the company's key constraint.

The broker viewed CTFE's funding needs remain unclear. It expected proceeds from CTF SERVICES' road asset monetization to be reallocated to the logistics and financial sectors for capital recycling, rather than being used for special dividend payouts. Without disposals of non-core assets, room for declaring special dividends is relatively limited.

The broker conservatively assumed recurring DPS will remain unchanged on a comparable basis in FY2026, but did not rule out upside potential due to strong cash flow. It also forecast adjusted EBITDA to grow by 4% annually in FY2027-28.

The broker remained positive on CTF Life and capital recycling. Although tax enforcement has tightened in mainland China, insurance demand remains resilient. AIA 's VONB rose 20% YoY in August to September, which also provides a positive read-through for CTF Life.

The broker maintained its Buy rating and HKD10.8 TP on CTF SERVICES.

data.title: Largecap rally has more room to run after strongest earnings in two years: DSP MF
data.description:
The rally in largecap stocks is likely to sustain, driven by global fund reallocation and the strongest quarterly earnings print in two years, according to Vinit Sambre, Head of Equities at DSP Mutual Fund, which manages nearly $27 billion in assets.

Sambre highlighted that the July-September quarter of 2026 (Q2FY27) results demonstrated robust performance across major sectors, including banks and commodities. This marks a shift from the previous eight quarters, which were largely dominated by broader market gains.

"I think this has been the strongest print in the last eight quarters, and especially including the largecaps as well," he said in a chat with CNBC-TV18.

The recent underperformance in mid and smallcap stocks represents a typical asset reallocation phase rather than a cause for concern. Once largecap allocations build investor confidence in the broader economy, capital typically cascades down to smaller companies where growth metrics remain strong.

Foreign institutional flows are expected to follow this earnings trajectory, chasing asset classes that offer visible, high-growth metrics as long as corporate earnings do not falter.

Addressing corporate governance, particularly regarding portfolio holdings like APL Apollo Tubes, he said the focus remains strictly on minority shareholder interests. Markets, he noted, increasingly differentiate valuations based on governance standards, rewarding well-managed businesses with a premium while penalising those that prioritise short-term metrics.

"For the companies who want to sustain high valuations, who wants to look at wealth creation long term, it is very pertinent beyond businesses that the key stakeholders for their businesses needs to be brought in parity with their own," Sambre stated.

data.title: Dollar lingers near 22-month peak as AI worries simmer; kiwi rises
data.description:
Key points:
  • NZ dollar rises as election result reduces political uncertainty
  • Risk-sensitive Aussie buoyed as Asian stock gains lift sentiment
  • Dollar garners support from expectations for Fed rate hikes

The US dollar hovered below a 22-month peak in holiday-thinned trading on Friday, with traders looking to equity markets for clues on direction as doubts about the AI trade trigger heightened volatility.

The New Zealand dollar rose after long-awaited results of the general election reduced political uncertainty, even with no clear winner. The Aussie dollar was also pulled higher by its neighbour.

The dollar index , which measures the currency against a basket of six peers, was steady at 103.74, at the end of a week that saw it pop to the highest level since March of last year at 104.53 on Monday only to erase those gains a day later. For the week, the index is currently down 0.1%.

The US currency was steady at 159.27 yen midway into Friday's Asian session, and has been pinned below 160 yen by worries of another round of Japanese intervention.

The greenback weakened 0.1% to 0.83435 Swiss franc .

The euro was little changed at $1.09725 and sterling gained slightly to $1.3118.

"All eyes are on whether the downtrend in AI-related stocks will turn around," Mizuho analysts wrote in a client note.

A recovery could see currencies such as the Aussie and high-yielding Mexican peso bounce back, while renewed selling would likely see those currencies under additional pressure, they said.

Japan's tech-heavy Nikkei share index gained 2% on Friday, while South Korea's KOSPI climbed 3.9%.

The risk-sensitive Aussie dollar added 0.4% to $0.66635, finding its feet after dipping to a one-year low of $0.6559 on Wednesday.

It also got support from a jump in the kiwi dollar earlier in the session, as results of the general election initially lifted the local currency as much as 0.6%. However, those gains later ebbed, and the currency was last 0.3% higher on the day at $0.5484.

New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon will seek the support of the centrist Opportunity Party to keep his ruling centre-right coalition in power after official results on Friday showed he fell just short of a parliamentary majority.

"NZD has risen slightly on the reduction — but not removal — of uncertainty, but the move is polluted by the USD effect," said Imre Speizer, Westpac's head of New Zealand market strategy.

"Risks of another breakdown remain, and we wouldn't rule out $0.5400 during the week ahead," he said. "Much of the bearish impetus has been due to the surging US dollar and hawkish Fed repricing."

The US currency has been supported by expectations for Federal Reserve policy tightening, with traders seeing a quarter-point interest rate hike on December 9 as a near certainty, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Hotter-than-expected US core personal consumption expenditures inflation in October, a sharp upward revision to third-quarter gross domestic product and a Federal Reserve survey showing continued economic growth and sticky inflation also have traders confident of an additional hike by around April.

The dollar index has risen about 5.7% so far in 2026, with only a month left in the year. The index is up 1.7% this month, putting it on track for its first run of three straight monthly gains since the final three months of 2024.

"The USD looks to be on a stronger-for-longer path than previously expected," NAB strategists wrote in a research report.

However, "given its rapid rise, we see limited scope for further gains," they added.

data.title: SG Mart, E2E Networks will not be included in the latest MSCI inclusion - Here's the reason why
data.description:
Global index provider MSCI has halted the inclusion of two Indian small-cap stocks, namely SG Mart and E2E Networks, ahead of their November 2026 index review, scheduled for implementation after market close on Monday, November 30, 2026, and effective from December 1.

Both companies had previously been identified as potential additions to the MSCI Global Small Cap Indexes. However, MSCI confirmed that neither stock will be added during this review cycle after both were placed on the Ineligible Alert Board due to domestic regulatory surveillance.

Why Will SG Mart, E2E Not Be Included?

Under Appendix I of the MSCI Global Investable Market Indexes (GIMI) Methodology, securities placed under India’s Short-Term or Long-Term Additional Surveillance Measures (ASM) framework are automatically disqualified from index additions during reviews.

Both the stocks are currently under Stage 1 of the Long-term ASM Framework.

Because inclusion in an MSCI index typically triggers substantial passive inflows from global exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and institutional trackers, missing the cut deprives both stocks of anticipated institutional liquidity.

SG Mart’s sudden placement under exchange surveillance and subsequent MSCI exclusion follows severe market turbulence across companies promoted by the Sanjay Gupta-led family, the founding group behind both SG Mart and APL Apollo Tubes.

Investors and proxy advisory firms (such as IiAS) raised sharp concerns over the deal's structure and valuation—specifically noting that Tata Steel Colors was being sold to APL Apollo at ₹16,300 crore, more than seven times its implied ₹2,200 crore valuation from late 2025.

The sell-off spilled directly into promoter-linked group entities. Coupled with SG Mart's own board meeting announcements regarding fundraising plans, SG Mart shares plunged—hitting a 20% lower circuit on November 25 before staging a partial rebound.

What Is The ASM Framework?

Introduced jointly by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) and domestic stock exchanges (NSE and BSE), the Additional Surveillance Measure (ASM) framework is designed to curb excessive speculation and alert investors to unusual trading activity.

For both SG Mart and E2E Networks, eligibility for MSCI index inclusion will now remain on hold until they exit the ASM framework and qualify again in a subsequent quarterly review.

Shares of SG Mart are trading 4% higher on Friday at ₹916.25. The stock is still up 140% so far this year.
